requirement_text: TOEFL internet-based score of 20 (scale 0-30) in written test and a total score of 90
source_authority_note: lunduniversity.lu.se is Lund University's official English-language site (website_url on the matched universities row is https://www.lu.se). Swedish national domain, fails looksOfficial(). Needs official-domain provenance, piece (A) of source-authority-gap.md.
limitations:
CONFLICTING EVIDENCE, unresolved by design. Two official sources describe the TOEFL requirement for the same Lund programmes differently.
(A) Lund University, this page, footer 'Last updated: 3 Feb 2026': "TOEFL internet-based score of 20 (scale 0-30) in written test and a total score of 90" -- legacy scales only, with no date bound of any kind.
(B) University Admissions in Sweden, the national operator that actually assesses English eligibility for Lund, https://www.universityadmissions.se/en/entry-requirements/english-language-requirements/: "For test results 21 January 2026 and later -- For English 6/English Level 2*: Total score of 4.5 (scale 1-6) with no section less than 4" AND "For test results 20 January 2026 and earlier -- ... Score of 20 (scale 0-30) in written test, total score of 90".
Neither side is chosen here. The lane's rule is that 'trust the newer page' has counterexamples in both directions, and this case has a live argument each way: (A) is the institution's own statement of its own requirement and was edited on 3 February 2026, i.e. thirteen days AFTER the ETS cutover, so its silence on the new scale is not obviously an oversight; (B) is the operator that performs the assessment and its two rows are exhaustive and mutually exclusive by date. A human who can ask Lund which one binds should resolve it.

SEPARATELY, and true regardless of how the conflict resolves: the '20 (scale 0-30) in written test' half has exactly the Glasgow defect documented in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md section 1. ETS supplies a comparable 0-120 OVERALL score for two years after the cutover, so the 'total score of 90' remains meetable, but section scores are reported on the 1-6 scale and are NOT restated on the old 0-30 subtest scale. A score report issued today therefore cannot satisfy the written-test half as published. Must evaluate to needs_manual_review, never not_met.
researcher_notes: Third confirmed instance of the partially-unsatisfiable TOEFL subtest pattern, after Glasgow and Bogazici. This one was found by the same whole-corpus scale check the earlier audit recommended, and is the first instance where an adjacent official source demonstrably gets it right -- which makes it a conflict rather than a lone defect.
